title: C-3 — Cost model snapshot
description:
The most load-bearing artifact. Divyansh Shukla (A) produces these; Aditya's live scheduler AND B's DES both consume them. This is where the two halves of the project actually meet.

Snapshots are kept as a time-ordered series per calibration campaign. The series was required for H3, which would serve the scheduler a snapshot from s seconds ago; H3 is out of paper one (research plan section 5), so paper one reads one named snapshot per node and the series stays for M12.

stochastic.autocorr_time_s is a measurement reported for characterisation (K6). The simulator does not read it: its noise is one lognormal multiplier per request with sigma from stochastic.sigma, independent across requests.

ON `form`: F-7 permits a lookup table OR a <=6-parameter regression. Pick ONE and commit at end of Week 2 — supporting both doubles B's interpolation logic for no research gain.

cost_model_schema.description: §12.2 mitigation: B's loader MUST reject unknown versions loudly rather than defaulting.

snapshot_id.description: e.g. cm_rtx3090_awq_20260428T1412Z. Referenced per-node from the run manifest (C-6).

node_class.description: F-9: with engine and quantization held constant, a node class is defined by hardware PLUS engine_config (F-9a) — e.g. 'rtx3090_ngl99_p4_q4km'. Two machines of the same hardware running different -ngl are different node classes and need separate snapshots.

form.description: F-7. Commit to one at end of Week 2.

prefill_ms_mean.description:
Mean of the engine-reported prefill span for this cell, in ms. Optional, and absent means the backend emitted no timings block for it.

It is here because prefill and decode do not respond to concurrency the same way, and a consumer that only has `service_ms_mean` cannot tell them apart. A simulator rescaling a request already in flight because the batch changed must not stretch the prompt evaluation: prefill is compute-bound and, under staggered arrivals, overlaps other requests' decode rather than their prefill.

READ THE CONCURRENCY COLUMN BEFORE USING THIS. The calibration grid holds `concurrency` requests in flight by firing them together, so at c>1 their prefills serialise against each other and this number carries that contention: 174 ms at c=1 against 592 ms at c=4 for the same 128-token prompt on the 1B GPU class. A Poisson workload does not synchronise arrivals that way and shows a flat ~180 ms at every batch size. The c=1 row is the uncontended prompt evaluation cost; the higher rows are a property of the calibration workload as much as of the hardware.

decode_ms_mean.description:
Mean of the engine-reported decode span for this cell, in ms. Optional, on the same terms as `prefill_ms_mean`.

Unlike prefill this one does behave across the grid: decode is memory-bound and per-request decode falls close to 1/c, so the value measured under synchronised arrivals matches what a staggered workload sees at the same batch size.

`prefill_ms_mean + decode_ms_mean` is not `service_ms_mean`. The difference is the engine's unattributed residual, which is kept rather than distributed.

stochastic.description: F-22: the DES service-time model MUST include a stochastic component fitted to observed throughput variance. The simulator multiplies each request's service time by exp(sigma Z - sigma^2 / 2), one draw per request, independent across requests, with no autocorrelation.

autocorr_time_s.description: tau, reported for characterisation (K6, MPR-1). The simulator does not read it. Meaningful only when `tau_resolved` is true: at the 5 s window floor it is a censored bound, not a measurement.

provenance.description: The settings that eliminate the confounds, made auditable from the results. Under F-9 engine and quant are constant across the pool, so engine_config is what distinguishes one node class from another.

engine.description: 'llamacpp' for every pool node class. 'vllm' only for the F-9b engine-gap probe.

engine_config.description: F-9a runtime parameters this snapshot was calibrated under. Must match the manifest's node block for any run that uses it.
